q: What's the valid priority range for custom NSG rules?
exp: Custom rules use priorities 100–4096; default rules sit at 65000+.

q: Which default inbound rule blocks everything not explicitly allowed?
exp: DenyAllInBound is the final default rule.

q: Which default rule allows Azure load balancer health probes to reach VMs?
exp: The AzureLoadBalancer service tag is allowed by default.

q: By default, can VMs reach the internet outbound under NSG rules?
opts: Yes — the default AllowInternetOutBound rule allows it
exp: Default outbound rules allow VNet and internet traffic (actual outbound connectivity still needs an outbound path).

q: Which CLI command creates an NSG rule allowing HTTPS from the internet?
opts: az network nsg rule create -g RG1 --nsg-name nsg1 -n AllowHttps --priority 200 --direction Inbound --access Allow --protocol Tcp --destination-port-ranges 443 --source-address-prefixes Internet
exp: Rules need a priority, direction, access, protocol, and ports and prefixes.

q: Which CLI command associates an NSG with a subnet?
opts: az network vnet subnet update -g RG1 --vnet-name VNet1 -n Web --network-security-group nsg1
exp: Subnet update with --network-security-group.

q: The subnet NSG allows inbound 443, but the NIC NSG has no custom rules. Can internet clients reach the VM on 443?
opts: No — the NIC NSG's default DenyAllInBound blocks it; both NSGs must allow
Yes — the subnet NSG is enough
exp: When both NSGs exist, traffic must pass both.

q: A subnet NSG denies outbound port 25. The NIC NSG allows outbound 25. Can the VM send SMTP on 25?
opts: No — outbound is evaluated NIC then subnet, and the subnet NSG denies it
Depends on priority numbers across NSGs
exp: Both NSGs must allow; the subnet denial blocks it.

q: Can you delete the default NSG rules?
opts: No — but you can override them with higher-priority (lower number) custom rules
exp: Default rules can't be removed, only overridden.

q: You want one NSG rule to allow traffic to several ports (80, 443, 8080). Is this possible?
opts: Yes — augmented security rules allow multiple ports and IP ranges in one rule
exp: Augmented rules support lists of ports and prefixes.

q: Which TWO can be used as the source of an NSG rule?
exp: Sources can be IPs/CIDRs, service tags, or ASGs.

q: An NSG rule should allow VMs to reach Azure SQL in West Europe only. Which destination?
exp: Regional service tags scope prefixes to one region.

q: A rule is changed from Allow to Deny while connections are active. What happens to existing flows?
opts: Existing connections may continue until they end; new connections are blocked
exp: Changes affect new flows; established flows may persist.

q: Order NSG processing for INBOUND traffic to a VM:
items: Evaluate the NIC NSG rules by priority
Evaluate the subnet NSG rules by priority
Deliver to the VM if both allow
exp: Subnet → subnet NSG → NIC NSG → VM.

q: Web VMs must accept 443 from the internet, and DB VMs must accept 1433 only from web VMs. Cleanest NSG design?
opts: ASGs 'asg-web' and 'asg-db'; rule 1: Internet → asg-web 443; rule 2: asg-web → asg-db 1433
exp: ASGs make role-based rules independent of IPs.

q: How do you put a VM into an application security group?
opts: Associate the VM's NIC (IP configuration) with the ASG
Add the VM to a resource group
exp: ASG membership is set on NIC IP configurations.

q: Answer Yes or No about ASGs:
stmts: A NIC can belong to multiple ASGs
ASGs can be used across VNets in the same rule
ASGs reduce the need to manage IP addresses in rules
exp: A NIC can join several ASGs; rule members must share a VNet; ASGs simplify rules; ASGs are regional resources.

q: Which managed service provides centralized, stateful Layer 3–7 filtering with FQDN rules and threat intelligence?
exp: Azure Firewall is a managed firewall-as-a-service. NSGs are basic L3/L4 filters.

q: Which subnet name does Azure Firewall require?
exp: Azure Firewall needs AzureFirewallSubnet, /26 minimum.

q: Which port must target VMs allow from AzureBastionSubnet for RDP through Bastion?
exp: Bastion connects to VMs over RDP/SSH privately.

q: Can one Bastion host reach VMs in a peered VNet?
opts: Yes — Bastion supports connecting to VMs in peered VNets
Only with Premium SKU and VPN
exp: Bastion works across VNet peering.

q: Which Bastion SKU is free, shared, and intended only for dev/test with one connection at a time?
exp: The Developer SKU is a free, lightweight option without a dedicated subnet.

q: Which Bastion SKU adds session recording and private-only deployment?
exp: Premium adds session recording and private-only Bastion.

q: Can you upgrade Bastion Basic to Standard?
exp: SKU upgrades are supported; downgrades require redeployment.

q: RDP should be open only on request, for 3 hours, from the requester's IP. Which feature?
opts: Just-in-time VM access (Microsoft Defender for Cloud)
exp: JIT opens NSG rules temporarily on approval.

q: Where do you enable a service endpoint?
opts: On the subnet (selecting services like Microsoft.Storage or Microsoft.Sql)
exp: Service endpoints are a subnet setting; the PaaS firewall then allows the subnet.

q: VMs should reach only ONE specific storage account through the service endpoint, not all storage accounts. Which feature?
opts: NSG rules with the Storage tag
exp: Service endpoint policies restrict endpoint traffic to specific resources.

q: When a VM uses a storage service endpoint, what source IP does the storage account see?
opts: The VM's private IP (subnet identity) instead of a public IP
exp: Endpoint traffic carries the private source IP and VNet identity.

q: After you enable a service endpoint, a storage firewall IP rule that allowed the VM's public IP stops matching. Why?
opts: Traffic now arrives with the private source IP, so you need a VNet rule instead of an IP rule
exp: Switch to VNet rules for subnets with service endpoints.

q: Which Azure service underlies private endpoints?
exp: Private endpoints are part of Private Link.

q: You publish your own app behind a Standard load balancer for consumers in other tenants to reach privately. Which feature?
exp: A Private Link service exposes your service; consumers create private endpoints to it.

q: On-premises clients must resolve a private endpoint's FQDN through a VPN. Recommended design?
opts: Forward the on-prem DNS zone for privatelink.* to Azure DNS Private Resolver (inbound endpoint) linked to the private DNS zone
exp: DNS Private Resolver lets on-premises DNS query Azure private zones.

q: A private endpoint connection shows 'Pending'. What's needed?
opts: The resource owner must approve the connection
exp: Manual approval is needed when the requester lacks permission on the target resource.

q: Answer Yes or No:
stmts: A private endpoint can be reached from a peered VNet
A private endpoint requires disabling the service's public endpoint
Private endpoints support NSG and UDR policies when network policies are enabled on the subnet
Each private endpoint maps to one specific resource (and sub-resource)
exp: Peered access works; disabling public access is optional; network policies for private endpoints can be enabled; endpoints map to specific resources.

q: Requirement: on-premises servers must reach Azure SQL Database privately over ExpressRoute, without public endpoints. Choose:
opts: Private endpoint for the SQL server
Public endpoint with a firewall rule
exp: Only private endpoints are reachable from on-premises.

q: Requirement: VNet VMs must reach a storage account with the least cost and no DNS changes, and the account's public endpoint can stay. Choose:
opts: Service endpoint plus a VNet firewall rule
exp: Service endpoints are free and need no DNS changes.

q: A VM resolves mystorage.blob.core.windows.net to a public IP even though a private endpoint exists. What's the likely cause?
opts: The privatelink.blob.core.windows.net private DNS zone isn't linked to the VM's VNet (or the VNet uses a custom DNS server without forwarding)
exp: DNS integration determines whether the private IP is returned.

q: Which Network Watcher feature diagnoses whether NSGs allow traffic between a source and a destination, showing every rule evaluated?
exp: NSG diagnostics evaluates rules across the path.

q: The 'Effective security rules' view is empty or unavailable for a VM. What's a common reason?
opts: The VM must be running to show effective rules
exp: Effective rules and routes require a running VM.

q: Which NSG flow log destination is used for analysis with Traffic Analytics?
opts: A storage account, processed into a Log Analytics workspace
exp: Flow logs land in storage; Traffic Analytics processes them into Log Analytics.

q: Microsoft is retiring NSG flow logs. What's the recommended replacement?
exp: VNet flow logs cover the whole VNet and replace NSG flow logs.

ctx: Subnet Web has nsg-web: priority 100 Allow TCP 443 from Internet; priority 200 Deny TCP 443 from 203.0.113.0/24. VM1's NIC has no NSG.
q: Answer Yes or No:
stmts: A client at 203.0.113.5 can reach VM1 on 443
A client at 198.51.100.7 can reach VM1 on 443
VM1 can reach the internet outbound under default rules
Another VM in the same VNet can reach VM1 on port 22 (by NSG rules)
exp: Rule 100 matches first for all internet clients, including 203.0.113.5, so the deny at 200 never applies; default outbound allows internet; AllowVnetInBound allows port 22 within the VNet.

q: In the previous scenario, how do you block 203.0.113.0/24 while allowing everyone else on 443?
opts: Give the deny rule a lower priority number than the allow (for example, deny at 90)
Add the deny to the NIC only
exp: The deny must be evaluated before the broader allow.

q: Which service adds adaptive tuning, attack telemetry, and cost protection against DDoS for public IPs in a VNet?
exp: DDoS Network Protection (or IP Protection) adds advanced mitigation on top of the default infrastructure protection.

q: Azure Firewall must translate inbound traffic from its public IP on port 3389 to a VM's private IP. Which rule type?
exp: DNAT rules translate inbound destinations.

q: Outbound web access must be allowed only to *.microsoft.com. Which Azure Firewall rule type?
exp: Application rules filter by FQDN.

q: Which TWO statements about service endpoints are true?
opts: They're configured per subnet and per service
They extend the VNet identity to the service
They give the PaaS resource a private IP
exp: Service endpoints are subnet settings that carry the VNet identity; they don't give private IPs or work from on-premises.

q: Order the steps to deploy Azure Bastion:
items: Create the Bastion resource (SKU, public IP)
Create AzureBastionSubnet (/26 or larger) in the VNet
Connect to a VM from the portal via Bastion
Make sure VM NSGs allow RDP/SSH from the Bastion subnet
exp: Subnet → Bastion → NSG check → connect.

q: Bastion is deployed in the hub, and VMs are in a peered spoke. Do the spoke VMs need public IPs?
exp: Bastion reaches VMs over private IPs across peering.

ctx: VNet1/SubnetA has a Microsoft.Storage service endpoint. Storage account st1 allows only SubnetA via a VNet rule. A private endpoint for st1 (blob) exists in SubnetB, with DNS correctly configured.
q: Answer Yes or No:
stmts: A VM in SubnetA can access st1 blobs
A VM in SubnetB can access st1 blobs through the private endpoint
An on-premises server over VPN can access st1 through the private endpoint (with DNS forwarding configured)
An on-premises server can access st1 through SubnetA's service endpoint
exp: The VNet rule allows SubnetA; private endpoint traffic isn't blocked by the firewall; on-premises can use the private endpoint; service endpoints don't extend to on-premises.
